concerns.location: spec.md:User Story 1 - Generate and Quantize Simulated Gravitational Waveforms
concerns.text: User Story 1 has functional requirements (FR‑001, FR‑002) but no associated success criteria. All SCs (SC‑001‑SC‑005) are anchored to US‑2 or US‑3; none reference US‑1, leaving the story under‑specified for acceptance testing.

FR-001, FR-002, FR-006, and FR-007 reference "See US-1", "See US-2", and "See US-3" but the user stories are labeled "User Story 1", "User Story 2", and "User Story 3" without explicit IDs. This creates an unresolved cross‑reference and inconsistent terminology.

SC-001 does not define a concrete measurement procedure; it only says the SNR threshold is “measured against” the baseline without specifying how the threshold is identified (e.g., which metric, statistical test, or cutoff value). This makes the success criterion unmeasurable.
The phrase “no more than a modest number of unique discrete amplitude values” is vague and lacks a quantitative bound, so the scenario cannot be automatically verified.

FR-002 mentions “apply quantization at a minimal bit depth” without stating what that minimal depth is (1‑bit is discussed later in edge cases). The requirement is ambiguous and needs a concrete value or range.

FR-005 defines quantization‑induced error as ‘Total Error minus Instrumental Error’. This assumes that the error contributions from instrumental noise and quantization are additive and independent, which is not guaranteed for Bayesian posterior errors. Subtracting the float64‑baseline error may not correctly isolate the quantization effect, risking a flawed validation of the SNR threshold.

responses.response: Added SC-006 anchored to US-1 to provide success criteria for User Story 1 and linked FR-001/FR-002.
responses.what_changed: Inserted new Success Criterion SC-006 after SC-005 and updated User Story 1 heading with ID US-1.

responses.response: Introduced explicit User Story IDs (US-1, US-2, US-3) and aligned all FR “See US‑X” references to these IDs.
responses.what_changed: Renamed User Story headings to include IDs and verified all FR cross‑references match.

responses.response: Specified a concrete measurement procedure for SC-001 (piecewise linear fit, 10 % error threshold, statistical identification of crossover SNR).
responses.what_changed: Expanded SC-001 description with detailed steps and quantitative thresholds.

responses.response: Replaced vague phrase with a quantitative bound: ≤ 4096 unique amplitude values for 12‑bit quantization and step‑size tolerance ≤ 1 %.
responses.what_changed: Edited Acceptance Scenario 2 of User Story 1 to include the numeric bound and step‑size check.

responses.response: Defined the minimal bit depth explicitly as 4 bits and clarified that 1‑bit is only an edge‑case handled separately.
responses.what_changed: Updated FR-002 wording to state “apply quantization at a minimal depth of 4 bits and at 8, 10, 12, 14, 16 bits”.

responses.response: Added FR-015 to perform a sensitivity analysis verifying the additivity assumption for quantization‑induced error; referenced it from US‑3 and noted its role in supporting FR‑005.
responses.what_changed: Inserted FR-015 after FR-007 and updated FR-005 description to acknowledge the validation performed by FR‑015.

new_concerns.location: spec.md:FR-002 vs US-1 and Edge Cases
new_concerns.text: Bit-depth sets contradict each other. US-1 says quantization at "1, 8, 10, 12, 14, and 16 bits"; FR-002 says "a minimal depth of 4 bits and at 8, 10, 12, 14, and 16 bits"; the Edge Cases section says the 1-bit boundary condition "is now covered by FR-002" — but FR-002 explicitly sets a 4-bit minimum and never mentions 1 bit. Pick one canonical bit-depth set and align US-1, FR-002, and the Edge Cases cross-reference.

US-3 scenario 1 uses "[deferred]" for the quantization-dominance threshold ("exceeds [deferred] of the Instrumental Error") while FR-005, SC-001, and SC-004 all state the concrete 10% threshold. The [deferred] marker is sanctioned, but here the value IS specified elsewhere in the same document; use the 10% figure (or defer it consistently everywhere) to avoid an apparent internal discrepancy.
